Getting started with rgoogleslides

Source: vignettes/rgoogleslides.Rmd
rgoogleslides.Rmd

Overview

rgoogleslides lets you create and modify Google Slides presentations directly from R. It talks to the Google Slides API v1 and uses gargle for authentication, which means you can share credentials with googledrive and googlesheets4.

Authentication

The first step is to authenticate. For interactive use, gs_auth() opens a browser window where you grant access to your Google account:

library(rgoogleslides)
gs_auth()

For automated / CI workflows, it is recommended to use a service account:

gs_auth(path = "path/to/service-account.json")

Creating a presentation 

id <- create_slides("My Report")
id
#> [1] "1abc..."

Adding slides

Build one or more requests with the add_*_request() family, then commit them all at once:

requests <- add_create_slide_page_request(predefined_layout = "TITLE_AND_BODY")
requests <- add_create_slide_page_request(requests, predefined_layout = "BLANK")
commit_to_slides(id, requests)

Inserting text 

requests <- add_insert_text_request(object_id = "<shape-id>", text = "Hello!")
commit_to_slides(id, requests)

Inserting a data table

create_data_table() is a convenience function that creates a table and fills it with a data frame in one call:

props <- get_slides_properties(id)
page_id <- props$slides$objectId[[2]]

prop <- page_element_property(page_id, width_magnitude = 600, height_magnitude = 300)
create_data_table(id, prop, head(mtcars))

Reading slide content 

page <- get_slide_page_properties(id, page_id)

page$get_tables()
page$get_text_boxes()
page$get_notes()

Replacing text globally 

requests <- add_replace_all_text_request(
  replace_text = "2026",
  text = "{{YEAR}}",
  match_case = TRUE
)
commit_to_slides(id, requests)
